meta.description:
MS0 calibration tables: load time, core loading cost, stranding cost, revocation exposure, notice thresholds and
individually rational (IR) contract prices per LLM tier, load-time scenario and contract of the default menu
(design/Sublet_design.md §1.5.3, §1.6, §3.6, §5.3.5, Table 3.8; open decisions Q24, Q25, Q29, Q30).
meta.catalog_note: MaaS entries (a10 proposed_catalog) are the default catalog (Q30): S, M, L with g = the instance-hour-weighted fused gpu_count (GPUs per replica by replica time) and L with 8-bit weights (16-bit weights do not fit on 8 x 80 GB); M_g_gpu_hours (g = 2), L_16bit (g = 16) and L_g4 (235B, g = 4) are sensitivity entries; the a5 Llama-3 tiers are the sensitivity catalog. g is measured on the trace's GPU mix, mostly GPUs larger than 80 GB; pricing it as H100-80GB is an assumption. Every entry fits on g x 80 GB (checks.catalog_fits_g_x_80GB)
meta.buffer_sample_size_caveat: MaaS buffers come from one week of slack; for D >= 120 min the P99 of many clusters is set by a single drop episode (sources.buffers gives the counts and the median ratio of P99 to the largest drop), so the MaaS IR prices of long windows (and the (C) threshold of the worst cluster) rest on one drop event (contracts.<k>.ir_summary.maas_p99_tail_episodes)
meta.rows_note: rows are at price reference maas_p99_median and the default 5-min slot; for the other price references and the 1-min slot use contracts.<k>.price_refs.<ref> (f_beta, H_star_mu_over_lambda, max_lambda_s_with_rho_le_2, a_usd_per_gpu_h) with load_time_s
meta.scope_note: H*_mu values come from C2, proven or checked only for tau = 0; every menu contract has tau >= 1 slot, so they are an approximation (design §1.5.1, Q12). Windows above 300 min (AEP-82-like notices of hours) are not in the menu and not priced here (a9b covers up to 24 h on its grid).

sources.a0, q_GPU, a_p: literature/sources/gpu-rental-prices-h100-2026-10.md (Silicon Data H100 index 2026-10-14: neo-cloud 2.85, hyperscaler 7.15 USD/GPU-h; AWS Capacity Blocks p5 5.97 USD/GPU-h); constants A0, Q_GPU, A_P of a5b_exposure_thresholds.py
sources.q_j: q_j = g q_GPU: fallback on hyperscaler GPUs of equal throughput (design §1.5.4, §5.3.5)
sources.mu_over_beta_tilde: ASSUMPTION, swept {0.2, 0.5, 1, 2} (design §1.5.5, Table 5.6, Q23; a5b MU_RATIOS)
sources.contract menu: ASSUMPTION: H in {0, 1, 2, 5, 10, 15, 30, 60, 120, 240} min, tau in {1 slot, 1 h}, plus one protected contract (design Table 3.7; Q29); slot 5 min by default, 1 min in the sensitivity run (design §1.5.1)
sources.buffers: a9_notice_buffer.buffer_curve on out/a1_slack_series.npz and out/a2_slack_series.npz (MEASURED; MaaS slack derived from allocation), quantile P99 (P99.9 as the sweep value), b_l(D) = running maximum of the raw quantile over all 5-min windows up to D (a9b `b_envelope_5min`; a9b `b_envelope` is the envelope over its 9-point grid only). Sample size: the MaaS series cover one week (2016 slots), so for D >= 120 min the P99 of many clusters is set by a single drop episode and lies just below the largest drop in the sample: at D = 60, 120, 240 and 480 min the P99 of 0, 9, 13 and 13 of the 20 clusters rests on a single drop episode, and the median ratio of P99 to the largest drop is 0.886 at 120 min and 0.926 at 240 min (a9b summary.maas_20_clusters.windows.<D>); per contract see contracts.<k>.ir_summary.maas_p99_tail_episodes
sources.IR price: a_lk = a0 / (1 - b_l(D_lender)), offered only if b < 1 (design §1.5.2, §5.3.5)
sources.H*_mu: a5b_exposure_thresholds.c2_hstar (C2-T4 formula; C2-SW substitution for a switch cheaper than beta~), status from c2/audit/out/model_switch_cost_default.txt and c2/audit/out/switch_cost_crossover.txt
sources.catalog: a10_maas_catalog.json proposed_catalog.entries.<entry>.{params_b, g, precision, w_GB} (params_b and g MEASURED on the trace's GPU mix, instance-hour-weighted medians, params_b over all online instances of the tier and g over fused instances; their use on H100-80GB GPUs is an ASSUMPTION; precision ASSUMED: 16-bit where the weights fit in 0.9 x 80 GB x g, 8-bit otherwise) and proposed_catalog.tiers.<S|M|L> for the shares
sources.a5 catalog: a5_reclaim_cost_calibration.json assumptions.weights_gb and assumptions.replica_hbm_GB / 80 GB per H100
sources.fit: every catalog entry has w_GB <= 0.9 x 80 GB x g (H100-80GB price unit; a5's usable HBM share), asserted

field_sources.lambda_s: load_time_s.<catalog>.<tier>.<scenario>: w / (bw * (g if per-GPU shards else 1)) + t_init (design §1.5.3)
field_sources.a (price): contracts.<k>.price_refs.<ref>.a_usd_per_gpu_h: a0 times the IR multiplier of the price reference
field_sources.beta_tilde_usd: beta_jl + lambda (g a + phi g q_GPU), lambda in hours (design §1.5.3)
field_sources.rho: 1 + beta~ / (g a D_pd) = 1 + f lambda / D_pd (design §1.6); 1 for the protected contract
field_sources.rho_le_2: rho <= 2, i.e. H in the platform's window accounting >= H*_beta (design §1.6)
field_sources.H_star_beta_s: beta~ / (g a) - tau = f lambda - tau (design §1.6); null for the protected contract
field_sources.H_star_mu_s: contracts.<k>.price_refs.<ref>.H_star_mu_over_lambda.by_switch.<default switch>.<mu>.value times lambda; null where C2 does not apply; status codes in H_star_mu_status_legend

H_star_mu_status_legend.PROVEN-Cor5: PROVEN (C2-Cor5, simple form) with switch cost beta~, for tau = 0; beta~ is not the switch cost of the full model (design §1.7.1 item 13)
H_star_mu_status_legend.PROVEN-T4: PROVEN (C2-T4 under (C')) with switch cost beta~, for tau = 0; beta~ is not the switch cost of the full model (design §1.7.1 item 13)
H_star_mu_status_legend.VERIFIED: VERIFIED NUMERICALLY: the exact game at the default prices (alpha = 0.3986) agrees with the formula (c2/audit/out/model_switch_cost_default.txt, bracket in `exact_bracket_over_lambda`); formula CONJECTURE, no proof (Q17); tau = 0
H_star_mu_status_legend.CONJECTURE: CONJECTURE: C2-SW formula at this alpha_k; the exact game ran only at alpha = 0.3986; tau = 0
H_star_mu_status_legend.NA-Cprime: not applicable: (C') fails, so up-front insurance attains 2 - alpha at every H (design §1.7.1 item 8)
H_star_mu_status_legend.+C-fails: suffix: (C) fails (alpha_k > 1/2), so no closed form of C2-Cor5 is proven even with switch cost beta~

S.source: a10_maas_catalog.json proposed_catalog.entries.S (instance-hour medians (params_b, fused g), window all; params_b and g MEASURED, precision ASSUMED)

M.source: a10_maas_catalog.json proposed_catalog.entries.M (instance-hour medians (params_b, fused g), window all; params_b and g MEASURED, precision ASSUMED)

L.source: a10_maas_catalog.json proposed_catalog.entries.L (instance-hour medians (params_b, fused g), window all; 16-bit weights do not fit on g x 80 GB; params_b and g MEASURED, precision ASSUMED)

M_g_gpu_hours.source: a10_maas_catalog.json proposed_catalog.entries.M_g_gpu_hours (M with the GPU-hour-weighted fused g (size-biased); sensitivity; params_b and g MEASURED, precision ASSUMED)

L_16bit.source: a10_maas_catalog.json proposed_catalog.entries.L_16bit (L with 16-bit weights and the memory-derived g on 80 GB GPUs (as a5 does for 405B); sensitivity; params_b and g MEASURED, precision ASSUMED)

L_g4.source: a10_maas_catalog.json proposed_catalog.entries.L_g4 (largest L mass point (235B, 0.4174 of L instance-hours) with its fused g; L median in the lender week; sensitivity; params_b and g MEASURED, precision ASSUMED)

warm_peer_rdma.label: LITERATURE (rate, t_init); ASSUMPTION (per-GPU shards)
warm_peer_rdma.source: zhang2025blitzscale p. 276 (summary.md): compute fabrics of 100-400 Gbps RDMA (low end used) and 'typical compute network setups (e.g., 200 Gbps per-GPU)', so each GPU loads its shard over its own link; t_init = CUDA context about 500 ms (zhang2025blitzscale §A.1, p. 293)
warm_peer_rdma.anchors: Mistral-24B to 6 prefill instances in 1.2 s (zhang2025blitzscale Fig. 21, p. 287); Llama-13B to 8 nodes in < 1 s (yu2025lambdascale p. 2)

ssd_optimized.label: LITERATURE (rate); load only
ssd_optimized.source: fu2024serverlessllm: LLaMA-2-70B (130 GB, p. 137) loads in 10.3 s from RAID0 NVMe (12 GB/s) with the ServerlessLLM loader (Fig. 6a, p. 144); checkpoint loading latency only, no engine start (§7.2, p. 144); scaled linearly in weight size (OPT-2.7B to OPT-66B: 0.5-10.0 s, Fig. 6a)

ssd_stock_safetensors.label: LITERATURE (rate); load only
ssd_stock_safetensors.source: fu2024serverlessllm: LLaMA-2-70B (130 GB, p. 137) with Safetensors from local SSD: 48.0 s (Fig. 6a, p. 144)

ssd_stock_pytorch.label: LITERATURE (rate); load only
ssd_stock_pytorch.source: fu2024serverlessllm: LLaMA-2-70B (130 GB, p. 137) with PyTorch from local NVMe: 84 s (p. 137; Fig. 6a, p. 144)

a5_10GBps.label: ASSUMPTION (a5 model); default pair with a5_2GBps (Q24)
a5_10GBps.source: a5_reclaim_cost_calibration.json assumptions.weight_load_gbps_GBps (10, local NVMe cache) and assumptions.engine_init_s (60)

a5_2GBps.label: ASSUMPTION (a5 model); default pair with a5_10GBps (Q24)
a5_2GBps.source: a5_reclaim_cost_calibration.json assumptions.weight_load_gbps_GBps (2, remote object store) and assumptions.engine_init_s (60)

cold_wan_10gbps.label: LITERATURE (link rate); lower bound at line rate
cold_wan_10gbps.source: 10 Gbps cluster network of fu2024serverlessllm (Fig. 10a, p. 146), where stock Ray Serve needed 213 s to start OPT-30B (p. 147); line rate, no engine start, so a lower bound

cold_wan_1gbps.label: LITERATURE (link rate); lower bound at line rate
cold_wan_1gbps.source: yu2025lambdascale p. 3: Llama-70B (140 GB) from a remote registry over 1 Gbps takes > 18 min; fu2024serverlessllm p. 148: KServe downloads OPT-6.7B over 1 Gbps in 114 s (first token 128 s); line rate, no engine start, so a lower bound

condition_C_at_IR_prices.definition: smallest lender window D_lender (5-min grid) at which the IR price a0 / (1 - b_p99(D)) gives alpha_k > 1/2, i.e. (C) fails; b is the 5-min envelope, so (C) fails for every longer window as well
condition_C_at_IR_prices.maas_p99_median_price_note: first window at which a0 x median IR multiplier / q_GPU > 1/2 (the multiplier of price_refs.maas_p99_median); null: none up to the longest menu window

spot_L7_p99_median.source: median over the 4 L7 spot pools, a pool that cannot offer counts as infinite
